title: Module 13 · Medication Safety and Florida Law
intro: ISMP high alert drugs, look alike names, Do Not Use abbreviations, weekly methotrexate, Joint Commission 2026 goals, error reporting and just culture, controlled substance diversion and DEA reporting, Florida CE and PDMP, discharge reconciliation.

cases.title: What makes a drug high alert?
cases.stem: You are learning the ISMP high alert list.

steps.q: Which of these are on the ISMP acute care high alert list?

options.t: Insulin
Heparin and other anticoagulants
Concentrated KCl and potassium phosphate injection
Tranexamic acid injection (added 2024)
Oral amoxicillin suspension
Ondansetron injection
Smart pump libraries and premixes
options.why: Standard concentrations matched to pumps; remove concentrated electrolytes from units.

options.t: Retraining staff after each error
options.why: Education alone is a weak fix (ISMP hierarchy).

options.t: Warning stickers on high alert vials
A new policy that staff must sign
options.why: Rules and policies are weak fixes.

cases.pearl: **High alert = big harm when wrong. Standardize, premix, pump library, separate storage.**

sources.t: ISMP (via ECRI): high alert medications in acute care settings (2024 list)
ISMP (via ECRI): ISMP updates high alert medication list (Jan 2024)

cases.title: Look alike, sound alike
cases.stem: Orders arrive for hydroxyzine and hydralazine on the same patient; another for "Celebrex" that the nurse heard as "Celexa."

steps.q: Which strategies reduce look alike and sound alike errors?

options.t: Tall man lettering (hydrOXYzine, hydrALAZINE)
Include the indication on orders
Separate storage and barcode scanning
Store them alphabetically side by side
Use brand names only on orders
options.why: Brand names also look and sound alike (Celebrex vs Celexa).

cases.pearl: **LASA: tall man letters, indication on the order, separate bins, scan.**

sources.t: ISMP (via ECRI): high alert medications in acute care settings (2024 list)

cases.title: Do Not Use abbreviations
cases.stem: During EHR downtime: "MSO4 2.0 mg IV q4h PRN" and "insulin 10 U QD."

options.t: MSO4 reads as magnesium sulfate: write morphine
Trailing zero: 2.0 can be read as 20
"U" can read as 0 or 4; "QD" as QID
"PRN" is on the Do Not Use list
"q4h" must be written "every 4 hours"
options.why: Acceptable, though spelling out is safest.

cases.pearl: **No U, IU, QD, QOD, MS, MSO4, MgSO4, trailing zeros. Always a leading zero.**

sources.t: Becker's: Joint Commission Do Not Use list

cases.title: Weekly methotrexate
cases.stem: Home med list: "methotrexate 15 mg daily." The patient has rheumatoid arthritis.

options.t: RA methotrexate is weekly; daily has killed
15 mg is above the RA maximum of 7.5 mg
options.why: RA doses often reach 15 to 25 mg weekly.

options.t: Methotrexate needs folinic acid daily
options.why: Folic acid is given; the frequency is the danger.

options.t: Nothing; daily is fine for RA
Confirm, then enter weekly with the day
options.why: Check with the patient and outpatient pharmacy.

options.t: Verify as daily, as written at home
Change to 2.5 mg daily to be safe
options.why: Still daily; confirm the real regimen.

options.t: Hold it and discharge without it
options.why: Clarify; do not drop the therapy.

cases.pearl: **Oral methotrexate for RA or psoriasis: weekly, with the day named.**

sources.t: ISMP (via ECRI): high alert medications in acute care settings (2024 list)

cases.title: Joint Commission in 2026
cases.stem: A surveyor asks how pharmacy supports the Joint Commission goals.

steps.q: What replaced the National Patient Safety Goals in January 2026?

options.t: 14 National Performance Goals
Nothing; NPSGs continue unchanged
A new set of 20 NPSGs for hospitals
CMS Conditions of Participation alone

steps.q: Which items fall under the medication management goal?

options.t: Labeling all medications on and off the sterile field
Reducing harm from anticoagulants
Order review, override review, standard concentrations
Antimicrobial stewardship
Hand hygiene compliance audits
Two patient identifiers before care

cases.pearl: **2026: National Performance Goals replaced NPSGs. Medications: label, anticoagulants, review, concentrations, stewardship.**

sources.t: Relias: Joint Commission National Performance Goals (replaced NPSGs January 2026)

cases.title: Reporting an error you made
cases.setting: Night shift · you verified a wrong dose
cases.stem: You verified a cefazolin dose meant for another patient. The nurse caught it before giving it.

options.t: Fix it, then report the near miss
Fix it and say nothing; no harm
Report only if the dose reached the patient
Tell the nurse to report it instead

steps.q: In a just culture, how is a human slip treated?

options.t: Console the person; fix the system
options.why: Just culture: console a slip, coach at risk behavior, act on reckless behavior.

options.t: Punish every error to deter others
Ignore all errors to protect morale
options.why: At risk and reckless behavior need action.

options.t: Suspend after a second human slip
options.why: Slips are consoled and the system fixed.

cases.pearl: **Report near misses, including your own. Just culture fixes systems.**

cases.title: Controlled substance discrepancy
cases.stem: A cabinet count is short two hydromorphone vials, and one nurse has far more wastes than peers.

steps.q: What does this suggest and what do you do?

options.t: Possible diversion: report per policy now
options.why: To the pharmacy manager or diversion team; do not investigate alone or confront.

options.t: Adjust the count and move on
Confront the nurse directly today
Wait for a third discrepancy first

steps.q: If theft or significant loss is confirmed, what does federal law require of the registrant?

options.t: DEA in writing within 1 business day; Form 106
DEA Form 106 within 30 days only
options.why: Initial written notice is within 1 business day.

options.t: DEA Form 41 within 1 business day
Board of Pharmacy only, within 7 days
Witnessed waste, documented in real time
Waste later, when it is convenient
Waste alone, then document the amount
Waste in the sharps container unwitnessed

cases.pearl: **Count off or odd waste patterns: report, do not confront. Theft: DEA within 1 business day + Form 106.**

sources.t: 21 CFR 1301.76: security controls, theft or significant loss reporting (eCFR)

cases.title: Florida license renewal
cases.stem: A Florida pharmacist is planning renewal.

steps.q: How often, and how many hours?

options.t: Every 2 years; 30 hours per renewal
Every year; 15 hours per renewal
Every 2 years; 24 hours per renewal
options.why: 24 extra hours apply to consultant pharmacists.

options.t: Every 3 years; 45 hours per renewal

steps.q: Which topics are required each renewal?

options.t: 2 h med errors, 2 h controlled drugs
5 h pain management and 2 h ethics
1 h HIV/AIDS and 2 h ethics
3 h immunization for every pharmacist
3 hours every 2 years if certified to immunize
24 extra hours for consultant pharmacists
A practical exam each renewal
An MPJE retake every 6 years
A new background check each renewal

cases.pearl: **Florida: 30 h every 2 years, 2 h med errors, 2 h controlled substances, no live hours since 2025.**

sources.t: Florida Board of Pharmacy: pharmacist renewal

cases.title: The PDMP (E-FORCSE)
cases.stem: A discharge opioid prescription will be filled at the hospital's outpatient pharmacy.

steps.q: What does Florida require of dispensers?

options.t: Report to E-FORCSE by close of next business day
Report to E-FORCSE within 7 days
Report to the DEA within 1 business day
options.why: DEA notice is for theft or loss.

options.t: No reporting for hospital discharges

steps.q: Why check the PDMP before filling?

options.t: Spot overlaps, many prescribers, high doses
It is only for law enforcement use
To confirm insurance coverage
To check the prescriber's DEA renewal

cases.pearl: **Florida PDMP (E-FORCSE): report by next business day; check before you fill.**

sources.t: St. Mary's medication safety, controlled substance and reporting policies (verify locally)

cases.title: Discharge medication reconciliation
cases.stem: A patient leaving after a GI bleed. Home list: aspirin, warfarin, omeprazole. Hospital: pantoprazole, warfarin held.

options.t: Each home drug: continue, change or stop
options.why: For example whether and when warfarin restarts.

options.t: Duplicates: omeprazole and pantoprazole
Follow up labs (INR) and who manages them
Restart all home drugs as before
options.why: Aspirin and warfarin after a GI bleed need decisions.

options.t: Nothing; discharge is the doctor's job

cases.pearl: **Discharge: every home drug gets continue, change or stop. No duplicates. Lab follow up named.**
